text:
ashley: Heads up — nightly ded10 run showed a regression in paged-attention memory behavior. At ~2h into the run we saw tail latency spikes and two OOMs on the 32k sequence workload. Dumped block-table stats and KV pager metrics :grimacing:

ashley: block_table: total_blocks=128k, free_blocks=6.2k, fragmented_bytes=1.9GB, slab_allocated=24GB, slab_waste_pct=7.9%

ashley: KV pager: pages_in_use=92k, hot_pages=58k, cold_pages=34k, page_faults/sec=420, avg_eviction_scan=3.2ms

devon: ugh. did we change slab size or the allocator path recently? :eyes:

ashley: no infra churn in the last canary; perf regression appears after merged FlashAttn-paged-variants PR (linked in thread). The profiler shows lots of tiny allocations in the block-table metadata path during long contexts.

maddy: can you paste the allocator flame sample? even a small snippet helps.

ashley: pasted minimal sample:

```
# flame top (alloc count)
block_entry_init  42.1%
kv_page_map_grow  18.3%
slotmap_insert     12.7%
slab_alloc_small   9.9%
compaction_scan    6.8%
```

ashley: suspecting that our per-request slotmap churn + opportunistic compaction is causing fragmentation; compaction runs bump into high concurrency and lose coalescing opportunities.

samir: two quick ideas — 1) make compaction randomized and cooperative (yield after N merges) to avoid long scans; 2) add an opportunistic background compactor thread that only runs when GPU utilization < 40%.

devon: +1 on background compactor. Also curious if changing slab bucket size from 4MB -> 8MB reduces fragmentation for long seqs. Worth AB testing on ded10.

ricky: what's the repro command? I can queue a dedicated run.

ashley: repro steps:
1) checkout nightly build from last green commit before FlashAttn-paged-variants merge
2) start ded10 image with --seq-max=32768 --concurrency=8 --batch=1
3) run long-query workload from /tests/long_context/ (script: run_long_context.sh) for ~3 hours

ashley: also tried running under valgrind/memcheck on a smaller run; fragmentation pattern shows many sub-4KB allocs that are never coalesced.

maddy: could be the slab splitting behavior — if we bias small-slab allocations to come from separate pool for metadata, we might avoid interleaving data and metadata which causes fragmentation. That plus a periodic full-scan compaction should keep slab waste bounded.

devon: I'll spin up two perf variants: (A) slab_bucket=8MB, compactor=background; (B) slab_bucket=4MB, compactor=aggressive (current). Compare slab_waste_pct, tail P99/P999 latencies.

infra-bot: Incident recorded: OOM on ded10-nightly (id: oom-1798039999-1). Logs archived to /s3/ded10/oom-1798039999.tar.gz

samir: also add telemetry for "fragmentation_events" (count when free_blocks< threshold && slab_waste_pct>5%). We should alert earlier instead of waiting for OOM.

ashley: good call. I'll add a short-term metric and a dashboard widget showing slab_waste_pct over time per-pool.

ricky: ping me when devon has the runs queued, I can reproduce locally quicker with a smaller data set.

devon: queued. PR with background compactor prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234 — it's rough but runnable. I'll attach perf logs once complete.

maddy: can we also gate the FlashAttn-paged-variants rollout on the compaction + slab tweak? rollback if P99 regresses > 20% vs canary.

ashley: yes, I'll open a rollback config and add the gating rule in rollout policy. For now marking as P0 perf investigation. :fire:

devon: estimated runs finish in ~2.5h. will report back in this thread with before/after numbers.

ashley: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. We'll sync tomorrow if needed.

samir: adding a short follow-up meeting: "Paged-attn slab fragmentation mitigation" — 30m tomorrow 10am PT.

ashley: link to test artifacts and full dumps: https://s3.company.internal/dumps/1798039999/ (contains blocktable dumps, kv pager metrics, and profiler samples)

devon: :thumbsup:

maddy: :eyes:
